title: Why AI Stock Images Get Rejected
subtitle: Learn the common technical and stylistic reasons stock agencies reject artificial intelligence imagery and how to fix them.
products: AI image prompt pack for stock sites
html:
Submitting AI-generated photos to stock photography platforms often leads to frustrating rejections. Reviewers examine these submissions closely for specific technical flaws that standard cameras rarely produce.

Understanding these rejection criteria helps you refine your prompt engineering and editing workflow. Here is a breakdown of why images fail quality control and how to correct them before submission.

Anatomical Errors and Extra Limbs

One of the most frequent rejection reasons is distorted human anatomy, such as extra fingers, floating teeth, or unnatural joint bends. AI generators often struggle with complex interactions between hands, faces, and objects.

To fix this, zoom in on your generated images at one hundred percent magnification before exporting. Use local editing tools to remove artifacts, or regenerate the image with more specific prompts focusing on hand placement.

Unnatural Textures and Artifacts

Stock reviewers look for sharp focus and realistic textures in skin, fabric, and foliage. AI images frequently exhibit a characteristic plastic sheen, overly smoothed skin, or background objects that blend illogically into one another.

Combat this by applying subtle film grain during post-processing and using upscale tools that preserve realistic surface details. Avoid heavy reliance on default smoothing filters that give subjects an artificial appearance.

Misspelled Words and Garbled Text

Images containing signage, labels, or documents often fail because the text appears as random gibberish or unreadable symbols. Stock buyers need clean, usable assets that do not require extensive cleanup of background typography.

The most reliable solution is to generate images with completely blank backgrounds in areas where text would normally appear. You can then add clean, legible typography manually using design software if the concept requires it.

Copyright and Trademark Violations

AI models are trained on vast datasets containing copyrighted characters, logos, and distinct architectural designs. Submitting an image that accidentally replicates a branded product or registered trademark results in immediate rejection.

Scrutinize every generated asset for hidden logos on clothing, recognizable consumer goods, or famous buildings. Crop out or paint over these elements, or prompt the generator to create generic, unbranded alternatives.

Preparing AI images for stock platforms requires a rigorous quality check rather than a simple drag-and-drop workflow. By removing anatomical errors, cleaning up background text, and ensuring realistic textures, you will significantly improve your acceptance rates.

Pick your best recent generation today and inspect it at full resolution for hidden artifacts before uploading it to your portfolio.
